title: SYNC: Measuring and Advancing Synthesizability in Structure-Based Drug Design
abstract: Designing 3D ligands that bind to a given protein pocket with high affinity is a fundamental task in Structure-Based Drug Design (SBDD). However, the lack of synthesizability of 3D ligands has been hindering progress toward experimental validation; moreover, computationally evaluating synthesizability is a non-trivial task. In this paper, we first benchmark eight classical synthesizability metrics across 11 SBDD methods. The comparison reveals significant inconsistencies between these metrics, making them impractical and inaccurate criteria for guiding SBDD methods toward synthesizable drug design. Therefore, we propose a simple yet effective SE(3)-invariant \textit{\underline{SYN}thesizability \underline{C}lassifier} (SYNC) to enable better synthesizability estimation in SBDD, which demonstrates superior generalizability and speed compared to existing metrics on five curated datasets. Finally, with SYNC as a plug-and-play module, we establish a synthesizability classifier-driven SBDD paradigm through guided diffusion and Direct Preference Optimization, where highly synthesizable molecules are directly generated without compromising binding affinity. Extensive experiments also demonstrate the effectiveness of SYNC and the advantage of our paradigm in synthesizable SBDD. Code is available at \url{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/SYNC-C94D/}.
problem: Designing synthesizable 3D ligands for protein pockets is hindered by lack of accurate synthesizability metrics and inconsistencies among classical metrics.
approach: Proposes SYNC, an SE(3)-invariant synthesizability classifier for SBDD and establishes a paradigm using guided diffusion and Direct Preference Optimization to generate synthesizable molecules.
contribution: SYNC demonstrates superior generalizability and speed compared to existing metrics; guided synthesis generates highly synthesizable molecules without compromising binding affinity.
